Hi all — attaching a quick pricing calc (Redwood_pricing_calc.xlsx) and summarizing assumptions below. Numbers below are conservative / likely / optimistic scenarios for effective $/1M tokens after caching impact.

Assumptions used in the calc:
- Base model cost (Redwood hosted, open model variant): $0.50 per 1k prompt tokens + $0.80 per 1k output tokens (list price for un-cached, baseline model)
- Pilot volume baseline: 100M tokens total
- Production volume baseline: 8B tokens total (we’ll run scaling scenarios)
- Prefix caching strategy: cache top 100k prefixes (by normalized token sequence) with 24h TTL; cache stores model outputs for prefixes to avoid prompt + generation cost on hits; assume we cache prompt+response for autocomplete flows (short responses).

Hit rate scenarios (prefix cache applies mainly to short/autocomplete traffic):
- Conservative: prefix hit 25%, KV reuse 5%
- Likely: prefix hit 45%, KV reuse 8%
- Optimistic: prefix hit 60%, KV reuse 12%

Effect on effective unit economics (example math, per 1M tokens requested):
- Uncached baseline cost (mix 60% prompt short/40% long): ~ $650 per 1M tokens
- Conservative (25% prefix hit): effective cost ~ $520 per 1M tokens
- Likely (45% prefix hit): effective cost ~ $360 per 1M tokens
- Optimistic (60% prefix hit): effective cost ~ $260 per 1M tokens

Notes on calculation:
- Prefix hits avoid both prompt & generation token billing in many cases (we model this as full saving on that request). For longer Q&A flows we model partial savings from KV reuse by reducing incremental generation tokens by the reuse percentage.
- We also include small infra cost for caching (RAM + eviction) baked into the per-1M calc (~ $0.02–$0.05 / 1M tokens).

Attached: Redwood_pricing_calc.xlsx (tabs: assumptions, pilot_calc, production_calc, sensitivity).
